title: Mode imperfections and displacement-controlled hyperelastic response
summary: Length-scaled mode transfer to stress-free geometry and accepted-state reaction curves; reuses existing nonlinear increment control.

science.statement: Length-scaled mode transfer to stress-free geometry and accepted-state reaction curves; reuses existing nonlinear increment control.

equations.label: Mode-shaped reference geometry
equations.description: Signed length amplitudes a_i multiply modes normalized at geometry nodes; j ranges over those nodes.

inputs.name: modes and amplitudes
inputs.description: Modes on the same mesh; zero modes rejected.

outputs.name: geometry receipt and accepted path arrays
outputs.description: Original coordinates retained; failed quality checks roll back.

assumptions: Response extraction requires a single hyperelastic material, ordinary strong boundary conditions and no external body/traction loads.
conventions: Each mode normalized by global maximum nodal vector norm; reference geometry is stress-free.
Signed reactions and boundary-averaged displacements from accepted snapshots.
limitations: No general arc length, snap-back, contact or elastoplastic path claim.
Rebuild nonlinear operators after geometry changes; preserve moving boundaries with facet tags.

validation_rules: Amplitude and restore checks on four cell topologies.
Defect-amplitude, mesh and increment sensitivity of guided column.

references.title: Abaqus eigenvalue buckling and imperfection-sensitive structures
